notes.title: Neural Speech Extraction with Human Feedback
notes.bp: A listener should extract a desired speech source from a mixture when ordinary separation assumptions are insufficient.
notes.wh: Target identity, mixture variability, and human preference can disagree with signal-level objectives.
notes.naive: Use an unconditioned separator and assume the loudest or most separable source is the desired one.
notes.ap: Use human feedback to guide neural speech extraction toward the target source.
notes.mech: Human preference supplies a target-selection signal alongside acoustic separation; the model is evaluated on extraction behavior.
notes.math: Separation is not only signal recovery: the system must specify which source counts as useful to a listener.
notes.eval: Separation is not only signal recovery: the system must specify which source counts as useful to a listener.
notes.ww: The paper reports neural speech extraction with human feedback.
notes.limits: Feedback population, mixture construction, target definition, signal metrics, and model scope bound transfer.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: LinearVC: Linear Transformations of Self-Supervised Features Through the Lens of Voice Conversion
notes.bp: Voice conversion should transform a speaker's voice while preserving linguistic content and remain useful with limited target data.
notes.wh: Self-supervised features encode both content and identity, so a simple transform can leak source traits or distort words.
notes.naive: Copy nearest target embeddings or train a separate waveform model per speaker.
notes.ap: Study linear transformations of self-supervised features as a controlled voice-conversion mechanism.
notes.mech: A learned transformation maps representation distributions toward a target voice while retaining content-related structure.
notes.math: Conversion is a representation-space mapping: content preservation and target identity are competing constraints.
notes.eval: Conversion is a representation-space mapping: content preservation and target identity are competing constraints.
notes.ww: The paper reports LinearVC results through the lens of self-supervised feature transformations.
notes.limits: Feature model, languages, target data, similarity/content metrics, and transform assumptions bound transfer.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: A Multimodal Chinese Dataset for Cross-lingual Sarcasm Detection
notes.bp: A multilingual ASR system should handle accents and varieties without treating one pronunciation norm as universal.
notes.wh: Accent variation changes acoustic-to-word evidence and can interact with language and speaker identity.
notes.naive: Train or evaluate only on standard speech and report one pooled error rate.
notes.ap: Analyze accent robustness under multilingual conditions and identify where recognition errors reflect a narrow training norm.
notes.mech: Subgroup and accent-conditioned evaluation separates intended-word performance across varieties rather than hiding failures in an aggregate.
notes.math: Robustness is a boundary measurement: the system's norm becomes visible only when varieties are evaluated separately.
notes.eval: Robustness is a boundary measurement: the system's norm becomes visible only when varieties are evaluated separately.
notes.ww: The paper reports a study of multilingual/accent robustness and its implications for ASR evaluation.
notes.limits: Accent labels, languages, speakers, test design, and subgroup denominators bound transfer.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.
